tags.qa_note: RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11 (deep QA pass). Re-pulled all prior sources plus scubaqua.com (second local operator) and atlantic-cable.com (specialist maritime cable-ship history database, via search). CONFIRMED: built 1954, Naples, Italy as CS Salernum (DAN's page spells it 'Selernum' but Divertrek, MyScubaDivingGearGuide, and atlantic-cable.com all agree on 'Salernum' -- treated as correct). CORRECTED/NEW: atlantic-cable.com confirms the ship was purchased by AT&T Corp. (via Transoceanic Cableship Co.) and renamed Charles L. Brown in 1984 -- this resolves the previously-unsourced 'renamed in 1984' claim. LENGTH CONFLICT FLAGGED: goldenrockdive.com/DAN/Divertrek/MyScubaDivingGearGuide give ~100m (320-327ft), but atlantic-cable.com's specialist ship-registry data gives 339.6ft (~103.5m) -- description now states sources report length between approximately 320 and 340 feet. Gross tonnage (2,789 GRT per atlantic-cable.com) is single-sourced and NOT included in the description per anti-hallucination policy (needs 2+ sources for historical/technical specs). Dropped the specific 'July 25, 2003' sinking date -- only the year 2003 is reconfirmed by 2+ sources this cycle. Depth reconfirmed 30-31m/100-102ft (Scubaqua: 31m/100ft; MyScubaDivingGearGuide: 31m/102ft). Starboard-side orientation reconfirmed by 3 sources. NEW: Golden Rock Dive Center describes a 30m/100ft swim-through through the structure -- added to profile. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: removed unconfirmed black/tiger grouper, green/spotted moray eel, lionfish, snapper-and-grunt schools, southern stingrays, and turtles-resting-on-deck (no source confirms these at THIS wreck). Confirmed replacements, each attested by at least one named operator/source: Caribbean reef sharks (DAN, Divertrek, Scubaqua), horse-eye jack schools (DAN, Divertrek, MyScubaDivingGearGuide), barracuda including a well-known resident nicknamed 'Charlie' (Golden Rock, MyScubaDivingGearGuide), cubera snapper (Golden Rock), spotted eagle rays and yellow-headed jawfish (Scubaqua).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11. French anchor details (c.1750-1775, over 3m long, over 1 ton) reconfirmed by Divertrek. CORRECTED: prior description implied a field of 'large iron anchors, chain segments, and ballast stones distributed across the reef slope' -- Divertrek's account describes ONE distinctive French anchor as the site's defining feature, not a scattered field of multiple anchors; description softened accordingly. Scubaqua (second independent operator, re-pulled today) confirms site at matching 18m/60ft depth and gives a site-specific marine life list: Spanish hogfish, drumfish, lobsters, Caribbean reef sharks, moray eels. A 2026 ScubaBoard trip report also lists the site (as 'Anchor Point North') among sites dived, corroborating existence/character without added detail. Removed previously-listed yellowtail snapper, blue tang, French angelfish, garden eels, and hawksbill turtles -- none confirmed at this specific site by current sources; replaced with the Scubaqua-confirmed list above.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11 -- SIGNIFICANT CORRECTIONS. Depth corrected from 10m to 17m: Divertrek and Scubaqua (two independent operators, re-pulled today) both give ~55ft/17m for the named dive site 'Blue Bead Hole', not the previously-recorded 1-10m. Entry type corrected from shore to boat: neither current source describes shore access; both list it among their boat-dive catalogs. Site type corrected from reef to muck: Divertrek describes a sand/grass-bed 'muck' dive and Scubaqua explicitly types it 'Muck/historical'. COLLECTION RULE CORRECTED: previous description stated collecting beads is illegal under STENAPA. This is WRONG -- Divertrek explicitly states blue beads are 'the only artifact divers may take home', and this is independently corroborated by uncommoncaribbean.com, which states blue beads are 'uniquely exempt' from the general no-collection rule that applies to all other Statia artifacts. Description corrected to reflect that beads (and only beads) may legally be kept. Bead origin (Amsterdam-made, pentagonal, Dutch slave-trade currency, thrown into the sea at emancipation) reconfirmed by lifeonthegoldenrock.wordpress.com. Marine life corrected to Scubaqua's site-specific list: pike blennies, scorpionfish, mantis shrimp, flying gurnards (flying gurnards independently corroborated by a separate general search result). Removed previously-listed brain/star coral, blue tang, parrotfish, sergeant majors, garden eels, flounder, and green sea turtles -- inconsistent with a muck/sand site and unconfirmed by current sources.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11. Composition (tugboat, barge, ship hull sunk in close proximity) reconfirmed across 3 independent sources including Scubaqua (second operator, newly re-pulled). Depth range refined to 18-20m: Golden Rock gives 20m/66ft, MyScubaDivingGearGuide gives 18m/60ft, Scubaqua's own page has an internal unit mismatch ('20m/60ft'); kept 20m as the JSON max, noted 18-20m range in the description. Marine life updated: added pipefish (Golden Rock) and octopus (Scubaqua); reconfirmed reef fish, angelfish, garden eels, Caribbean stingrays, juvenile fish habitat. REMOVED unconfirmed 'groupers and moray eels in the hull structures' -- no current source attributes these to this specific site.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11. DIFFICULTY CORRECTED from Intermediate to Beginner -- Golden Rock Dive Center's own site page rates Hangover Reef as Beginner, and Scubaqua lists it at OWD (open-water) level; no re-pulled source supports Intermediate. Depth range 10-17m (30-60ft) reconfirmed across Golden Rock, Scubaqua, and a PADI-sourced site summary. MARINE LIFE REWRITTEN to the confirmed, cross-corroborated list: queen conch and spiny lobster (Golden Rock + Scubaqua), hawksbill turtles (PADI summary + a 2026 ScubaBoard dive-report thread naming a hawksbill 'featured prominently'), horse-eye jacks and permit, yellowhead jawfish, peacock flounder, angelfish, longlure frogfish and longsnout seahorse (PADI-sourced summary). REMOVED unconfirmed copper sweepers, glassfish clouds, bar jacks, banded coral shrimp, and green moray eels -- not attested by any current source for this site; these appear to have been generic padding in the prior description. Dropped scubaverse.com as a validation source (see destination-level note on its reliability).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11. SOURCE SET REPLACED: previously cited goldenrockdive.com, divertrek.com, and wearestatia.com no longer mention Crooks Castle by name on re-pull (Golden Rock's current 9-site page does not list it at all). Re-validated instead against PADI's dive-site database and Zentacle, both of which give matching coordinates (17.47445, -62.98887 vs. our 17.4744, -62.9889) and matching stats: reef, boat access, beginner, max depth 32.8ft (~10m) -- exact match to existing data, no change needed. STENAPA's own park page (statiapark.org) confirms Crooks Castle by name as a site where 'there is always a sea turtle or stingray hanging around'. SOFTENED unconfirmed artifact specifics: 'ballast stones' and 'ceramic fragments' are not corroborated by any current source (only weathered cannons/stonework and onshore ruins are, per a local history blog and STENAPA context); language adjusted to avoid overstating unconfirmed detail. MARINE LIFE NARROWED to what STENAPA specifically attributes to this site (sea turtles, stingrays) -- removed French/queen angelfish, spotted drums, yellowhead jawfish, reef squid, and frogfish, none of which are confirmed for this site (PADI's 'sharks, whales, dolphins, turtles' tag is identical boilerplate applied to multiple unrelated site pages and was not treated as site-specific evidence).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11. Depth tightened to 17-18m (Golden Rock and Scubaqua both give 18m/60ft; Divertrek gives 55-60ft). DATING CONFLICT FLAGGED: general sources describe two 18th-century wooden merchant vessels, but Divertrek specifically identifies the recovered anchor as an English Admiralty Longshank type dated to the early 19th century -- this conflict is now written into the description rather than silently resolved. NEW (single-sourced, flagged as such): Divertrek reports one anchor was buried by Hurricane Irma (2017). MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: Divertrek and Scubaqua both specify GREEN turtles (not hawksbill as previously written) -- corrected. Southern stingrays reconfirmed by 3 sources. Added seahorses, frogfish, blennies (Scubaqua). Removed unconfirmed moray eels and French/grey angelfish. VESSEL NAMES: the claim that the two wrecks are 'Charles Brown' and 'Berkeley Springs' (18th-century British naval vessels) traces to a single source, scubaverse.com's generic St Eustatius dive-guide page -- and that same page separately references 'Hilma Hooker', which is a Bonaire wreck, not a Statia site. This strongly suggests the scubaverse.com dive-guide page mixes in non-Statia content and is unreliable. The vessel-name claim is now flagged as unverified and likely spurious rather than merely 'unconfirmed'; scubaverse.com has been dropped as a validation source destination-wide.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11. Nurse sharks and lettuce sea slugs reconfirmed by Golden Rock. Dropped scubaverse.com (reliability concern, see Double Wreck note) and replaced with padi.com and a 2026 ScubaBoard trip report as the second and third independent sources -- both list Nursing Station by name; a PADI-sourced summary adds squirrelfish schools hovering near sponge-dotted overhangs and notes several 18th/19th-century anchors are also present at this site. Kept Intermediate difficulty (Golden Rock rates it 'Beginner to Intermediate'; wall/overhang topography and current potential support the higher end). MARINE LIFE EXPANDED with corroborated sightings: hawksbill and green turtles, spotted moray eels, Caribbean spiny lobster, southern stingrays (multiple diver reports via the PADI/ScubaBoard aggregation) alongside the Golden-Rock-confirmed nurse sharks and lettuce sea slugs.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-11 -- UNRESOLVED FOR 3-SOURCE BAR. Re-pulled all three cited sources: none currently mention 'Five Fingers South' by name or give site-specific depth/type/marine-life detail (Golden Rock's current 9-site page does not list it at all). A PADI dive-site page for plain 'Five Fingers' exists (coordinates 17.46376, -62.98059, close to but not identical to our 17.465, -62.9833) but gives only a generic 'Marine Reserve: Reef' classification with the same boilerplate 'Sharks, Whales, Dolphins, Turtles' tag applied to unrelated site pages -- not treated as site-specific confirmation. Per policy, NOT padding with weak sources to manufacture a third domain. validated left as-is (true, reflecting the original curated entry); no factual changes made to depth/difficulty/site_type since no new site-specific evidence was found either supporting or contradicting the existing curated values. Flagged in QA summary as needing further destination-specific research (e.g. a direct site visit, a currently-updated operator page, or a ScubaBoard thread naming this exact site) before it can be considered independently re-verified.
